item.title: Ice storm warnings in effect across Mississippi, Alabama, Tennessee, and Georgia
item.description: Ice storm warnings are in effect for parts of Mississippi, Alabama, Tennessee, and Georgia between January 24 and 26, 2026. Ice accumulations of 6 mm to 25 mm (0.25 to 1 inch) and wind gusts up to 30 mph (48 km/h) are forecast across the regions. The combination of freezing rain, sleet, and gusty winds is expected to cause widespread power outages, tree damage, and extremely hazardous travel conditions. Source

item.title: Moscow sends heavy equipment to deal with historic snow emergency in Kamchatka
item.description: Moscow sent two military cargo planes to deliver heavy snow-clearing equipment to Kamchatka on January 22, 2026, after historic snowfall claimed two lives last week. More than 2 m (7 feet) of snow fell in the first half of January, followed by another 3.7 m (12.1 feet) in December, burying entire homes and paralyzing the region. Source

item.title: Long-duration power outages and extremely hazardous travel expected as major winter storm spreads from the Southern Plains to the Northeast
item.description: The National Weather Service (NWS) warns of catastrophic ice accumulation from the Southern Plains to the Southeast as a major winter storm develops and tracks northeastward from January 23 to 26, 2026. The storm is forecast to produce widespread freezing rain, heavy snow, and dangerously cold temperatures, threatening critical infrastructure and travel across much of the eastern United States. Source

item.title: Potentially historic winter storm forecast to impact more than 30 states across the U.S.
item.description: A potentially historic winter storm associated with the Polar Vortex is forecast to bring heavy snow, freezing rain, and dangerous cold across much of the United States from January 23 to 26, 2026. The system is expected to cause widespread travel disruptions, power outages, and hazardous conditions from Texas to the Northeast, with more than 200 million people under various National Weather Service warnings and watches. Source

item.title: Avalanche claims 9 lives in Pakistan’s Chitral District
item.description: An avalanche claimed nine lives and injured a 9-year-old child of the same family in Pakistan's northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province on Friday, January 23, 2026. Source

item.title: Severe snowstorm leaves 11 dead in Afghanistan
item.description: Heavy winter storms struck northern and central Afghanistan on Thursday, January 22, 2026, causing avalanches, building collapses, and road blockages across several provinces. At least 11 people were confirmed dead, with fatalities reported in Kandahar, Parwan, Bamyan, Maidan Wardak, Jawzjan, and Faryab. Source

item.title: Landslide claims 9 lives and leaves over 80 missing in West Bandung, Indonesia
item.description: At least nine people have been reported dead, while over 80 remain missing, in Indonesia after a major landslide destroyed homes and forced evacuations in the Pasir Langu village on January 24, 2026. Source

item.title: Rare auroral glow detected within South Atlantic Anomaly during January 19 severe geomagnetic storm
item.description: Severe geomagnetic storm on January 19, 2026, generated a rare auroral glow inside the South Atlantic Anomaly, a region where Earth’s magnetic field is significantly weaker. Photographers in Brazil captured a diffuse purple band over Cambará do Sul during peak geomagnetic activity, documenting the latest in rare instances of possible auroral or SAR arc activity within the anomaly. Source

item.title: Stratospheric warming developing over the Arctic forecast to weaken the polar vortex and influence February weather
item.description: Meteorological forecasts show a major sudden stratospheric warming event forming over the Arctic, likely to cause significant weakening of the polar vortex in early February 2026. The resulting atmospheric disruption may alter jet-stream dynamics and increase the risk of Arctic air intrusions into North America and northern Europe during the second half of February. Source

item.title: Episode 41 eruption at Kīlauea produces 480 m (1 575 feet) fountains, tephra reaches Hilo and Puna, Hawaii
item.description: Episode 41 of Kīlauea’s ongoing Halemaʻumaʻu eruption began at 11:10 HST (21:10 UTC) on January 24, 2026, producing lava fountains up to 480 m (1 575 feet) high and the broadest verified tephra dispersal of the current summit eruption sequence. Fine ash and Pele’s hair were carried by easterly winds to communities as far as Hilo and coastal Puna, while coarse fragments up to 30 cm (1 foot) fell near the vent. The eruption ended abruptly after about eight hours of activity. Source
